title: Scribe a shelf's end to an out-of-flat wall: hold the shelf and run a pencil compass along the wall
instruction: Holding the shelf against the wall, scribe its end to the wall: run the compass from the shelf's front edge to its back edge in one unbroken line, point on the wall, pencil on the shelf, then put the compass down off the shelf and wall.
context: Walls are rarely flat, so a shelf, countertop or cabinet side that must fit tight to one is scribed: set against the wall, a locked compass is run along it with its point on the wall and its pencil on the board, legs square to the wall, and the pencil copies the wall's line onto the board; cut to that line, the board fits with no gap. A compass that twists or leaves the wall, or a board that drifts, copies the line wrong. Done by: carpenters, including finish carpenters and cabinet and countertop installers (O*NET 47-2031.00: "Measure and mark cutting lines on materials, using a ruler, pencil, chalk, and marking gauge.").
setup: Millimetres. Positions on the table top, forward (x) from the line through the two arm bases and left (+y) or right (-y) of the midline; arm bases 610 apart. 1) Wall section, fixed: 25 MDF on edge, 260 long (x = 100 to 360), 100 tall, painted matte white, its face toward the robot's right routed to a listed profile (two humps and a hollow): the face stands out from the line y = 212 toward the shelf by the offset tabled every 5 mm in the README (-1.16 to +3.98, so the face runs y = 208.0 to 213.2), back flat at y = 233, screwed to a 19 MDF foot 70 deep (y = 233 to 303) clamped to the table. 2) Shelf, free: planed pine 1x6 (eastern white pine), 19 x 140 x 300, 0.32 kg, flat on the table, length along y, its square-cut end against the wall. The trial seed mod 4 sets the layout: front edge at x = 120, 147, 174 or 201 (back edge 140 further); end at y = 207.97, 207.97, 208.38 or 208.38, touching the wall where it stands out most along that stretch (0.05 gap). 3) Pencil compass, free: General Tools 843/1 class wing-nut pencil compass and scriber (brass-plated steel, hardened steel point, 9 x 9 square knurled top grip), a 60 HB pencil stub in its clamp, locked so the pencil line is 10.0 from the wall side of the point, point 2 above the pencil tip, 168 overall, 26 g. 4) Stand, fixed: pine base 50 x 50 x 19 (y = 130 to 180) and 20 x 20 post, 132 tall to a steel fork (two tines 6 wide, 42 long, 8 apart, each with a 6 wide notch between two 1.5 high steps at the centre) opening toward the robot's right, fork centre at x = 80, y = 110. The compass hangs by its hinge knuckle (10 across, 14 long) in the notches, legs down, point leg toward the wall, pencil tip 8.9 above the table. Nothing else is on the table. The README lists the wall profile, each layout's targets and every collider. Friction (estimates): pine 0.5 static / 0.4 dynamic; painted MDF 0.5 / 0.4; compass 0.25 / 0.2, its knurled grip 1.0 / 0.9.
scoring: Stations: 14 lines square to the shelf's end, 7, 17, ..., 137 from its front edge. At each, the reading is the pencil line's distance from the shelf's end to the line's centre: a steel rule graduated in 0.5, zero end butted on a square block held to the end, read under a 10x loupe to 0.1 (in simulation, from the lead's recorded path). Repeated marks: crossings of a station within 1 of each other read as one band, at its centre; crossings more than 1 apart leave the station unmarked; a single touch counts within 0.25 of a station. Target: 10.0 minus the wall's gap from the shelf's end at that station (README table per layout, or feeler gauges before the trial). Bend: each layout has three gate stations named in the README; no line credit unless all three are marked and the middle reading lies at least 1.5 off the straight line through the outer two, on the target's side (a straight line fails on every layout). One unbroken line: follow the line from the front edge to the back edge (0 to 140 across the shelf's depth), through the marks read at the stations; measure with the rule each unmarked stretch it crosses (straight across the board from the end of one mark to the nearest point of the next, and from each edge to the line's nearest end). The longest is the gap; it must be at most 2.0 (README says why), so separate touches at the stations, dashes or a line stopping short of an edge get no line credit. Line credit (gap at most 2.0 and bend met): 1.0 if all 14 within 0.5 of target; 0.5 if at least 12 within 1.0; 0.25 if at least 10 within 2.0; else 0. Finished: the compass put down clear of the shelf and the wall (its bounding box at least 2 from theirs; hung on its stand does this), every gripper TCP at least 30 from the compass's and the shelf's bounding boxes, the compass slower than 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s and the shelf slower than 2 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s. Score: 1.0 = line credit 1.0 and finished for the last 1 s; 0.75 = line credit 1.0 but not finished (compass held, on the shelf or moving, or a hand on the shelf); otherwise the line credit (0.5, 0.25 or 0). Sticky 0 for the rest of the trial: the shelf moved more than 30 across the table from its start, or the shelf or compass more than 20 below the table top. Success is 1.0.
reset_notes: Use zero object jitter. The trial seed mod 4 picks the layout (README). Erase the line or use a fresh face or board; lay the shelf flat with its end touching the wall at the layout's position; hang the compass on its stand, point leg toward the wall. The compass stays locked at 10.0: check it with a caliper each session. The scorer's pencil record and its 1 s window start fresh each trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The pencil marks wherever its tip is within 0.2 mm above to 2 mm below the board's top face (no force threshold); drawn dots (faint in the 320 x 176 videos) cover only the 17 mm next to the end; the score uses the recorded path. The wall face is a triangle mesh with 2 mm facets; the point does not dig into the paint. The compass is one rigid body locked at 10 mm; its leg, pin and grip sizes and all frictions are estimates. Stand and wall are fixed to the table.
